name: Fivetran
license: Proprietary; the Python Connector SDK is MIT
summary: Managed connectors that copy data from SaaS apps, databases and files into your warehouse or lake, billed by the rows that change each month.
intro: Fivetran is a hosted service that copies data from sources into a destination you own. You pick a connector (a SaaS API such as Salesforce, a database, files), give it credentials, and choose a destination: Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks, PostgreSQL and others, or its Managed Data Lake Service, which writes Parquet files with Iceberg metadata to S3, ADLS or GCS. The first sync copies all history. After that, incremental syncs run on a schedule (every 6 hours by default, every minute on the top plans) and fetch only what changed, from API cursors or, for databases, the change log, such as PostgreSQL’s write-ahead log. Fivetran keeps the cursors and checkpoints, creates and alters destination tables as the source schema changes, and adds columns such as `_fivetran_synced` and `_fivetran_deleted`. Transformation happens afterwards in the warehouse, usually with dbt. With Hybrid Deployment, the data is processed inside your network while Fivetran’s cloud orchestrates it.

Pricing is measured in Monthly Active Rows (MAR): the distinct rows, by primary key, inserted, updated or deleted in a calendar month, counted per connection and table. A row that syncs many times in a month counts once, and history from the initial sync is free. The price per MAR falls as a connection’s volume grows, and since March 2025 those tiers apply per connection rather than across the account. Fivetran’s own Standard-plan examples, checked 6 October 2026: a Google Ads connection at a median 88,240 MAR costs $48.67 a month, Marketo at 847,574 MAR costs $424.54. Fivetran merged with dbt Labs on 1 June 2026, and both brands continue.
strengths: More than 700 managed connectors: you configure them instead of writing and running extraction code
Log-based CDC for databases (PostgreSQL logical replication, and HVR for large Oracle and SAP replication)
Handles schema drift: new columns and tables appear in the destination unless you block them, and soft-delete and history modes keep deleted rows and old versions
Initial historical syncs don’t count as paid MAR, and the Free plan covers 500,000 MAR a month
Writes to every major warehouse or to Iceberg tables in your own object storage, and Hybrid Deployment keeps processing inside your network
limits: Bills are hard to predict: a job that touches every row of a big table makes all of them active for the month, and since January 2026 deletes and every history-mode version count too
Volume discounts build up per connection since March 2025, and each connection with 1 to 1 million MAR carries a $5 base charge, so many small connections cost more than their rows suggest
Reverse ETL is priced far higher per row: Fivetran’s median example is $202.25 a month for 12,007 activated MAR (Snowflake to Salesforce), against $22.06 for 34,479 MAR of Facebook Ads
Closed source with fixed connectors: unusual sources need the Python Connector SDK, and leaving means rebuilding every pipeline elsewhere
Fast syncs are plan-gated: Standard goes down to 15 minutes; 1-minute syncs and cron schedules need Enterprise or Business Critical

snippet.title: A custom connector with the Connector SDK: Fivetran stores the cursor and merges rows
source: from fivetran_connector_sdk import Connector, Operations as op
cursor = state.get("updated_since", "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z")  # state is empty on the first sync
op.upsert(table="invoices", data=invoice)  # merged on the primary key
op.checkpoint(state={"updated_since": cursor})  # the next sync resumes here

sections.title: How the bill is built
sections.intro: List prices aren’t published per MAR; the pricing page shows examples and a calculator. These are the rules that decide what you pay.

items.name: Monthly Active Rows
items.text: Each distinct primary key inserted, updated or deleted in a month, tracked separately per connection and table. A row counts once a month however often it syncs. Tables without a key get a `_fivetran_id` computed from the row’s values.

items.name: Per-connection tiers
items.text: The rate per MAR falls as volume grows, but the tiers apply to each connection on its own, not to the whole account. Fivetran said this would be a price cut for most customers; accounts with many small connections lose pooled discounts.

items.name: Base charge
items.text: Every standard connection with 1 to 1 million MAR in a month costs at least $5, except on the Free plan.

items.name: Deletes and history mode
items.text: Deletes count as paid MAR. In history mode, which keeps every version of a row, repeated updates to the same row in one month each count.

items.name: What’s free
items.text: Initial historical syncs, re-syncs of rows identical to the destination, history backfilled when you add a column, and connection trials.

items.name: Transformations
items.text: The first 5,000 model runs a month are free on every plan; then $0.01 per run up to 30,000, $0.007 up to 100,000 and $0.002 beyond.

items.name: Free plan
items.text: 500,000 MAR for connections, 5,000 model runs and 3,500 MAR of reverse ETL (Activations) a month.

items.name: Annual contracts
items.text: Committing to a year gives automatic discounts that grow with the annual list price: 5% at first, rising to 22.6% for contracts above $145,340 a year at list price.

items.name: Airbyte
items.text: Connectors for APIs, databases and files into warehouses and lakes, self-hosted or as a cloud service.

items.name: Meltano and Singer
items.text: Taps and targets that pass JSON over a Unix pipe; Meltano runs and configures them as code.

items.name: Estuary and Artie
items.text: Streaming change data capture from databases into warehouses with low latency, for when hourly batches are too slow.

items.name: Cloud-native options
items.text: AWS DMS and zero-ETL integrations into Redshift, Google Datastream and BigQuery Data Transfer Service, and Fabric Data Factory copy jobs and mirroring.

story: George Fraser and Taylor Brown, friends since childhood, founded Fivetran in 2012 and went through Y Combinator’s winter 2013 batch with a data analysis tool for scientists. In 2014, responding to what customers needed, they built their first connector. The bet that followed was that moving data should be a utility: managed pipelines from each source that copy everything into a cloud warehouse, where analysts transform it with SQL afterwards.

Cheap cloud warehouse storage made copying raw data reasonable, and Fivetran priced by the rows that change each month. In 2021 it raised $565 million at a $5.6 billion valuation and bought HVR for $700 million, adding high-volume database replication for systems such as Oracle and SAP. In 2025 it agreed to buy Census, a reverse ETL company, and bought Tobiko Data, maker of SQLMesh and SQLGlot. That October it agreed an all-stock merger with dbt Labs, its partner for a decade; the deal closed on 1 June 2026, with Fraser as CEO and dbt’s Tristan Handy as president.

choices.choice: Fixed, managed connectors instead of a toolkit
choices.why: Writing and maintaining extraction code for every SaaS API was the most time-consuming part of a pipeline. Fivetran builds and runs each connector, and customers only configure it.
Storage became cheap enough to keep untransformed copies, so Fivetran loads source tables as they are and leaves modelling to SQL in the warehouse.

choices.choice: Bill by rows changed, not by data volume
choices.why: Monthly Active Rows count each changed row once a month, and history from the initial sync is free, so the price follows how much the source changes rather than how big it is.
Source APIs add fields all the time. By default new columns and tables are created in the destination, so pipelines keep running instead of failing on schema drift.

timeline.text: George Fraser and Taylor Brown found Fivetran
Builds its first connector; opens headquarters in Oakland
Raises $565M at a $5.6B valuation; buys HVR for $700M
